title: Filming: Mary Had A Little Lamb by Wings | 1972
content:
Wings filmed four promotional clips for their second single, ‘Mary Had A Little Lamb’, on 13 May 1972.

They had flown from Machrihanish airport in Scotland to London on 11 May, and two days later headed to Television Centre in Southampton.

Earlier in the month, Paul McCartney had invited director Nicholas Ferguson to High Park Farm in Campbeltown to discuss the shoot. Ferguson suggested they employ Michael Wield as a set designer.

Ferguson and Wield constructed four sets for the films: a grassy knoll, circus tent, barn, and blue screen. The idea was to create multiple clips that could be shown on a range of TV shows to promote the single. The lighting was by Joe’s Lights.

I was well aware of [the need for] discretion. I arranged with Southern Television that I wanted nobody in the building at all except our crew, so they had complete secrecy. It’s common knowledge that they all smoked joints, but I wanted that to be completely discreet – if they want to smoke a joint, they can smoke a joint… It was a very relaxed atmosphere, very easygoing, everything went to plan. There was no temperament with anybody because they all seemed happy with what we were doing.
Nicholas Ferguson, 9 March 2022
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73, Allan Kozinn, Adrian Sinclair

The films were vision mixed during filming, so no editing was required. During the week ahead, McCartney and Ferguson reviewed the footage at a post-production facility in Soho, London.

The first of the films was the barn promo, which appeared on the BBC’s Top Of The Pops on 25 May 1972. The grassy knoll clip was shown on the BBC’s Basil Brush Show on 24 June, and the special effects promo was first shown in the US on the Flip Wilson Show on 12 October.

The circus clip remained in the vaults at MPL until it was released in 2018 on the Archive Collection reissue of Red Rose Speedway.
